Brief facts gleaned from Final Report filed along with DAR would reveal that Bablu Kumar driving Motorcycle No.DL-9SBU-7235 with Smt. Seema Devi riding the pillion, on their way from Keshopur Mandi to Mohan Garden, Uttam Nagar, met with an accident near the cut of Road No.235, DAV School, Vikaspuri, New Delhi on 23.03.2021 at around 2:20 pm after Mahindra Champion No.DL1LQ-2854 coming from opposite side at very high speed in rash and negligent manner collided against their motorcycle.

They were taken to DDU Hospital, New Delhi where nature of injury upon MLC No. 2891/2021 of Seema Devi was opined simple whereas nature of injury upon MLC No. 2890/2021 of Bablu was opined grievous.
3. FIR No.138/2021 under section 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Vikaspuri on 24.03.2021 and notice under section 133 of M.V. Act was served upon Regd. Owner Byas Kumar who informed that Dalip Singh was driving the vehicle at the time of accident.

Motorcycle No.DL-9SBU-7235 and Mahindra Champion No. DL-1LQ-2854 seized by the IO were released on superdari after their mechanical inspection and documents including RC & policy of offending Mahindra Champion were verified from concerned authorities.
Dilip Singh (driver) was formally arrested on 25.03.2021 and released on police bail and offence under section 338 IPC was added on the basis of final opinion upon MLC of injured Bablu.
Separate Kalandra under section 5/180 M.V Act was prepared against Byas Kumar (Regd. Owner) after Dalip Singh failed to produce valid and effective licence for driving the vehicle.
IO, thereafter concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in MACT No.643/2021 Bablu Vs. Dalip Singh & Ors.

It is apposite to note that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in MACT No.643/2021 Bablu Vs. Dalip Singh & Ors.

Himachal
Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
20 . Following observations in para 15 of aforesaid judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court being relevant are extracted herein below :
"15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a praticular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimaints were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied...."

21. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.

sentences.text: CONVEYANCE AND SPECIAL DIET 28.
A sum of Rs.60,000/- each is stated to have been incurred on conveyance and special diet.
Treatment record Ex.PW-2/1 (Colly.) reveals that injured Bablu Kumar having suffered bodily injury in road accident on 23.03.2021 continued to visit DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, Delhi till 13.04.2021.
It is assumed that he might have used private vehicle/hired taxi for undergoing treatment till 13.04.2021.
A sum of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) is therefore awarded towards conveyance.

Injured Bablu Kumar might have also needed special diet for full and complete recovery from swelling, pain, tenderness over left leg AND 'Minimally Displaced Fracture Involving Distal Shafts of Both Tibia & Fibula' and is awarded Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) towards special diet.
ATTENDANT CHARGES 29.

It is assumed that Bablu Kumar having suffered swelling, pain and tenderness over left leg, pain in right foot AND 'Minimally Displaced Fracture Involving Distal Shafts of Both Tibia & Fibula'
might have needed an attendant to assist him for around two months even if such gratuitous service was rendered by some or the other of his family/relatives.

Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Kumari Lalita 1982 SCC Online Delhi 123 has held that the victim cannot be deprived of compensation towards gratuitous service rendered by some of his family member.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
18. Respondent Dalip Singh (driver) despite being indicted of rash and negligent driving of Mahindra Champion which hit the motorcycle near the cut of Road No.235, DAV School, Vikaspuri has not entered witness-box for disputing rash or negligent driving and adverse inference is required to be raised against the driver as per the dicta of Hon'ble High Court of Orissa in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Durdadshya Kumar Samal & Ors. 1987 SCC Online Ori. 57 AND Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Vs. Smt. Kamlesh & Ors. decided by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi on 11th November, 2008.
19. It is apposite to note that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in MACT No.643/2021 Bablu Vs. Dalip Singh & Ors.
Injured Bablu Kumar is therefore not entitled to be granted any compensation under the head - Medicines & Treatment.
27. It is well settled law that compensation for future medical expenses is to be granted only in serious cases of injury where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof as held in paras 6 & 7 of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (Supra).
Injured Bablu Kumar is therefore not entitled to compensation towards MACT No.643/2021 Bablu Vs. Dalip Singh & Ors. Page No. 10 of 20 future medical expenses in the absence of prescription verifying need for further treatment and cost thereof.
Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Kumari Lalita 1982 SCC Online Delhi 123 has held that the victim cannot be deprived of compensation towards gratuitous service rendered by some of his family member.
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 9 of Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Co.
Ltd. & Anr. (2010) 10 SCC 254 has observed that whole idea in case of assessment of all damages for personal injury is to put the claimant in the same position as he was insofar as money can.
Perfect compensation is hardly possible but one has to keep in mind that the victim has done no wrong; he has suffered at the hands of wrongdoer and Court must take care to give him full and fair compensation for that he had suffered.
34. Compensation for (i) loss of future earning/prospects AND (ii) non pecuniary damages including loss of amenities and loss of expectation of life is not required to be assessed in the absence of serious injury resulting in permanent physical disability.
There is nothing on record to justify withholding interest on the award amount.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the present case, it will be just and proper to grant interest @ 7.5%
per annum on the award amount in terms of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Mannat Johar & Anr. (2019) 15 SCC 260.
2008 (5) SCC 107 for contending transfer of ownership and vicarious liabilty shifting upon the possessory owner who had the control over the vehicle.
Respondent HDFC Ergo General Insurance Co. will therefore be entitled to recover compensation amount with interest from Dalip Singh (driver) AND Byas Kumar who being owner/insured cannot escape from his liability so long as the vehicle is registered in his name as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in (i) Dr. T.V. Jose Vs. Chacko P.M. Alias Thankachan and Others (2001) 8 SCC 748; (ii) Anamika & Ors. Vs. Jai Pal Singh & Ors. 2023 ACJ 2015 AND (iii)
Bablu vs Dalip Singh And Anr on 7 February, 2025
Surendra Kumar Bhilawe Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. (2020) 18 SCC 224.
40.
